2. **Organize research directions**

     - As simple, minimal, and atomic as possible but not trivial

     - If progress is relatively early, prioritize feasible, easy-to-implement ideas with long-term promise.

     - Otherwise, balance ambition and implementation feasibility
     - The chosen/best idea MUST explicitly address at least two user-facing failure modes identified in the User Diagnosis. If it does not, it is NOT eligible to be selected, regardless of improvements on model-diagnosis metrics.
     - The chosen/best idea MUST explicitly address at least one model-facing failure modes identified in the Model Diagnosis. If it does not, it is NOT eligible to be selected, regardless of improvements on user-diagnosis metrics.

5. **Write the report in Markdown**  
   For the selected idea, include:
   - A synthesis of insights and proposed directions  
   - The structured framework of existing methods and the new algorithm  
   - A list of new ideas with their assessment scores
   - Detailed description of the chosen/best idea, including rationale, pseudocode, and implementation notes

The report must be focused, technically accurate. Being concise with 200-500 words without trivial and redundant information.
Support all claims with evidence and references, and remain tightly aligned with the target problem.

 ## Search results
Recent work supports separating persistent preferences from current intent. MSMT-LSI (2024) uses separate long/short attention networks with multiple temporal embeddings; [hierarchical preference modeling (online 2025)](https://journal.hep.com.cn/fcs/EN/10.1007/s11704-025-41181-y) adds dynamically routed long-term interest vectors, selects those matching short-term intent, and fuses them with time encoding. [DSRec (September 2026 preprint)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.21548) is especially relevant: historical aggregation for stable interests, a local-intent branch whose state evolution depends on time gaps, and residual cross-fusion between branches. These mechanisms motivate adaptive alternatives to a fixed five-item residual, but do not establish gains on the pinned four-category benchmark.

Separate branches alone do not establish disentanglement. [CLSR](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.13090) supplies an earlier practical template: history-derived long/short interest proxies, contrastive supervision, adaptive aggregation, and counterfactual evaluation. For SASRec, a lightweight experimental inference is to combine the existing representation with several causal decay pools and a learned gate conditioned on observed history and elapsed gaps. Interest states remain latent hypotheses; histories cannot establish users’ conformity or diversity traits.

Controlled comparisons matter: [Spotify’s October 2026 study](https://research.atspotify.com/2026/10/do-sequential-recommendation-benchmarks-require-higher-order-sequence-modelling) reports pairwise-transition models beating both Transformer reproductions on four of five benchmarks. Proposed ablations: fixed versus learned mixing, one versus multiple timescales, and real versus constant/shuffled gaps while holding item order and positions fixed. For deletion probes, compare preserving original position indices against compacting the sequence. Select using the common macro validation HR@10; these controls test predictive contributions without claiming causal recency effects.

---

Evidence supports testing objectives before changing representations. [gSASRec (2024 extended abstract)](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/939) attributes SASRec weaknesses partly to overconfidence from sampled BCE and proposes generalized BCE. [Sampled-softmax analysis (2024)](https://wujcan.github.io/papers/tois-ssm.pdf) identifies informative negative gradients and top-K ranking benefits. [Correcting LogQ (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331) revisits sampling correction: the designated positive is always included, unlike sampled negatives; treating both identically introduces bias. Correction must match the actual sampling construction, particularly with popularity-distributed in-batch negatives.

Hardness requires control. [Enhanced BPR (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.19276) explicitly addresses false negatives that mislead hard-negative training; [adaptive hardness sampling (2024)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28709) investigates adapting difficulty rather than always choosing the hardest item. These findings motivate—not establish—a uniform-plus-moderately-hard mixture, warm-up, and masking known training positives. Unknown future preferences remain unobservable; high model scores alone cannot establish whether an item is a true negative.

For this benchmark, a useful controlled ablation is unchanged SASRec with multi-negative sampled softmax, generalized BCE, then a controlled hard-negative mixture, comparing all four categories under matched GPU budgets and fixed macro validation HR@10. Electronics’ weaker margins do not identify the cause. Keep the host’s 99-negative evaluator unchanged: [sampled-metric research](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) shows sampled evaluation can reverse model rankings relative to full-catalog evaluation. Therefore, validation gains support this candidate protocol, not automatically better full-catalog recommendations.

Strongest lightweight match: [Revisiting Graph Projections (2025)](https://arxiv.org/html/2506.09209v1) combines normalized user–item graph projection with directed, inverse-distance-weighted purchase transitions; recommendations come from weighted graph neighbors, without pretrained weights. Important limitation: its sparsity regularizer uses product-category transitions, unavailable here. A training-only item-transition variant is feasible; replacing category smoothing with title/description clusters would be an experimental adaptation. The paper explicitly treats temporal relationships as a proxy for complementarity, not verified relationship labels.

Two relevant architectural ideas: [SComGNN (AAAI 2024)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28734) combines low-pass and mid-pass graph filters to capture both relevance and dissimilarity, suggesting that ordinary similarity smoothing can miss complementary relationships. [TransGAT (ICDM 2024)](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10884336/) encodes behavioral direction and jointly learns complementary/substitute graphs. Its reliance on relation graphs limits direct transfer when only chronological histories and text are available.

Suggested hypothesis to validate: retain SASRec personalization and add a gated directed-transition score, using separate source/target item embeddings trained from scratch. Compare immediate versus short-window transitions, symmetric versus asymmetric scoring, and optional TF–IDF or learned bag-of-words title/description features for sparse items. These are proposed adaptations, not established findings from the cited papers. Text similarity should provide auxiliary evidence rather than automatically identify substitutes; purchase order likewise cannot establish compatibility or complementarity.
